name: n2n_v2
_comment_sensor: TWO DIFFERENT THINGS. `sensor` is the model's identity: stage() writes denoise_{sensor}_v1.onnx and the S30 Pro is the camera Nocturne targets, so the shipped file is unchanged. `sensors` is the training MATERIAL. n2n_v1 used one key for both and so trained on 29% of the archive -- 5596 of 8408 frames are S50 -- and the S50 groups are the deep ones (M42 2361 frames, SH2-142 1357, NGC7023 821).
_comment_weighting: Measured on the finished n2n_v1 set (2026-08-24): 85% of its tiles had an input of fewer than 128 frames and the rungs matching how the user actually shoots (239/256/301/395) were 6.5% between them. Nobody chose that -- the ladder makes one rung per power of two, every group can afford the shallow end, only the biggest can afford the deep end, and a flat pairs_per_depth replicates the shallow rungs once per group. So: pairs per RUNG. shallow_depths is one rung per octave rather than all seven, because keeping every power of two below 128 at one pair each still leaves shallow material near a third of the set. Shallow is kept, not weighted towards: a brand-new Seestar owner does have a 30-frame stack.
_comment_pairs_per_depth: v1's flat `pairs_per_depth` is deliberately absent: with a per-rung count every rung now carries its own, and leaving the old key here would read as though it still controlled something.
